earlier_scan.source_named: Njantcho Kouagang, Elisabeth. 2018. A grammar of Kwakum. Doctoral dissertation, INALCO/Leiden (408 pp; Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description). Full text not located online; Hare 2018 DIU theses (read) contain no stress statement.

sources.citation: Njantcho Kouagang, Elisabeth. 2018. A grammar of Kwakum. PhD thesis, INALCO / Sorbonne Paris Cite. 409 pp. (HAL tel-02175417)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Ch.2 (segmental phonology, syllable structure, phonotactics, non-prepausal vowel deletion) and Ch.3 (tone: underlying H vs L vs zero, mora as TBU, tone movement, downstep) contain no statement on word stress or accent; 'accent' occurs only for tone diacritics. Notes NW-Bantu stem-initial consonant asymmetries (half the consonants restricted to C1) and that a stem-initial TBU must be /H/ or /L/ (never toneless), but never frames this as stress/prominence.

sources.citation: Hare, Stacey A. 2020. Kwakum Orthography Guide. Journal of Language, Culture, and Religion 1(1): 13-48; and Hare, D. & S. Hare 2020, Introduction to the Kwakum People and Language, JLCR 1(1): 1-12 (whole issue PDF).
sources.note: Nothing. Sec.3 'Tone': lexical and grammatical tone, three underlying levels H, M, L combining into contours on long vowels; orthographic tone-marking decisions. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Hare, Stacey A. 2018. Tone in Kwakum (A91) with an application to orthography. MA thesis, Graduate Institute of Applied Linguistics (Dallas International University). xxv+299 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on Kwakum stress. Phonological sketch (consonants, vowels, syllables) plus tone analysis: three contrastive tones L, M, H, mora = TBU, contours mainly on long vowels, floating tones. Cites Hyman on stem-initial vowel stability; summarises Belliard 2005 as placing contour tones on stem V1 or word-finally. 'Prominent syllables' appears only in a Yip 2002 quotation about Bantu generally.

sources.note: Nothing. Sec.2 covers vowels, consonants, vowel deletion, phonotactics (stem-initial onset licensing, 'prosodic stem' in reduplication) and tone; no stress/accent statement.

sources.note: Known only through Hare 2018:30, who reports that the ms. treats final-vowel deletion as tone-conditioned and quotes its p.4: 'Vowel deletion can be predicted from the tone of the final vowel..In some data, vowel deletion takes place only when the tone of the vowel is low. In contrast, there is no deletion when it is high.' It therefore presupposes Njantcho's lexical H vs L (vs zero) analysis of Kwakum tone with the mora as TBU; it is not an independent statement of the tone inventory and no copy was located to read.
